messages:
aj: Heads up — after the CUDA 12.20p1 + cuBLASLt roll last night we're seeing a reproducible p50/p95 latency regression for small-batch (bs=1) short-sequence requests. Not a network blip, looks like kernel selection is picking a different GEMM path that uses a larger workspace and higher launch overhead.

aj: Quick numbers from canary: seq=16, bs=1 on A100: p50 went 11.8ms -> 26.7ms, p95 34ms -> 72ms. Throughput for tiny-batch generation down ~1.6x.

aj: Repro recipe: 
```
./tools/perf_runner --model gpt2-xl --batch 1 --seq 16 --warm 50 --iters 200 --cuda 12.20p1
```
Captured nvprof/Nsight traces show switch from tiled-f32-gemm (fast small-ws kernel) to workspace-heavy algo with extra global memset.

sophia: omg, I saw a blip in prod dashboards at 02:12 too. Did you bisect to a specific artifact (driver vs cublaslt vs triton)?

aj: Started bisecting this morning. Narrowed it to the stack: CUDA 12.20p1 runtime + cuBLASLt 3.x on top of our Triton build. When we force-select the old algo with cublasLt heuristics override we get previous numbers back. So heuristics change in cuBLASLt looks suspicious.

aj: Minimal repro where we toggle heuristics:
```
# env override we used in canary
export CUBLASLT_ALGO_PREF=legacy_small_ws
./perf_runner --model ...
```
When set, p50 returns to ~12ms.

maria: CI has a perf test failing: perf/smallbatch-latency on nightly. I queued a quick canary rollback to the previous cuBLASLt to see if it stabilizes. Will post the rollout ticket.

ci-bot: build/ci/perf/nightly #482 failed: perf/smallbatch-latency — p50 increased by 130% (regression threshold 15%). Link: https://ci.internal.redwood/job/482

eric: Any chance our autotuner in the runtime is mis-ranking kernels due to a change in reported workspace size? We saw similar behavior last year where an upstream lib started returning different winsize hints and our selector favored the wrong kernel.

aj: Good point. I dumped the kernel metadata returned by cuBLASLt and there's a new field (workspaceInBytes estimate) that is larger for what used to be the small-ws kernel. Our selector logic sums workspace + launch_overhead and that pushes it above the threshold, so we pick a different kernel.

sophia: Can we short-term add a compatibility patch that ignores the new workspace hint for small shapes? If it's just a regression in the vendor heuristics that seems safest while we engage cuBLASLt.

maria: I'm preparing a rollout block: reverting cuBLASLt to 3.7.x on the canaries + pinning the driver version for dedicated until we confirm fix. Filing support ticket with vendor now (ticket RED-9876).

aj: Filed bug + data dump in RED-9876. Attaching nvprof snippets, kernel metadata JSON, and the perf-runner command output. Also added a short script to force legacy selection if teams want immediate mitigation.

eric: For the longer term we should harden our kernel selector: 1) cap weighting on workspace hint for small-ws kernels, 2) add a fuzz-test harness that simulates upstream heuristic changes, 3) add config flag to prefer lower-latency kernel for bs<=2.

sophia: +1 to the selector change. I'll open a small RFC and a PR for the cap.

maria: Rolling back on canary now, will monitor dashboards for the next 30m. If stable I'll push rollback to next tier and block the 12.20p1 rollout.

ci-bot: rollouts/canary revert cuBLASLt -> 3.7.9 started by maria at 1767894370

aj: Thanks — will keep bisect artifacts pinned in the ticket. If vendor responds with a patch we can test their fix against our harness before re-rolling. :face_with_monocle:
